definitions.explanation: Traditional handicrafts made by ordinary people for everyday use, valued for their simple beauty and functionality rather than fine-art status. Also refers to the aesthetic movement that promoted such crafts.

notes:
Short for {民衆的工芸|みんしゅうてきこうげい} (popular crafts). The term was coined by {柳宗悦|やなぎむねよし} (Yanagi Muneyoshi) in the 1920s as part of the Mingei movement, which celebrated the beauty of ordinary, handmade objects used in daily life — pottery, textiles, woodwork, and lacquerware made by anonymous craftspeople.

CULTURAL NOTE:
The Mingei movement drew attention to the aesthetic value of simple, functional objects. {日本民芸館|にほんみんげいかん} (Japan Folk Crafts Museum) in Tokyo is the movement's flagship institution. Many regional souvenir shops sell {民芸|みんげい}{品|ひん}.

- {民芸|みんげい}{品|ひん} — folk craft item, folkcraft product
- {民芸|みんげい}⟦{店|てん}→店：10011_ten⟧ — folk craft shop
- {民芸|みんげい}⟦{運動|うんどう}→運動：00821_undou⟧ — the Mingei movement
- ⟦{伝統|でんとう}→伝統：09585_dentou⟧{民芸|みんげい} — traditional folk crafts
